title: Check yourself: while and do-while loops

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A sender walks a batch by index: `int k = 0; while (k < batch.size()) { Msg m = batch.get(k); if (m.isHeartbeat()) continue; send(m); k++; }`. A batch holds four messages, and the third is a heartbeat. What does the sender do?

options.text: It sends two messages, then reads index 2 again forever, since continue returns to the condition with k still at 2
options.says: continue goes straight back to the condition; k++ is an ordinary statement of the body, so it is skipped and k stays on the heartbeat

options.text: It sends two messages, then stops at index 2, since continue ends the whole loop with k still at 2
options.says: continue ends only the current pass and returns to the condition; it doesn't leave the loop

options.text: It sends three messages, then stops at index 4, since continue moves k on to 3 before the condition
options.says: that is what continue does in a for loop, whose update is part of the loop; in a while loop the update is a statement of the body, and continue skips it

options.text: It sends three messages, then stops at index 4, since k++ is the loop's update and runs after every pass
options.says: a while loop has no update of its own: k++ runs only on the passes that reach it

origin.section: continue in a while Loop Jumps to the Condition, Past the Update at the Bottom

questions.stem: At shutdown a worker runs `do { archive(inbox.poll()); } while (!inbox.isEmpty());`. `poll()` returns null when the queue holds nothing. This time the inbox is already empty at shutdown. What happens?

options.text: archive is called once, with null, since the body runs before the condition is first tested
options.says: a do-while makes its first pass before the test, so on empty input it handles one null

options.text: archive is called again and again, with null, since the condition stays true while the inbox is empty
options.says: the condition is !inbox.isEmpty(), which is false for an empty inbox, so the loop stops after the first pass

options.text: archive is never called, since the condition sees the empty inbox before the body runs
options.says: that describes a while loop; a do-while tests after the body

options.text: archive is never called, since poll() on an empty queue ends the loop before archive runs
options.says: poll() returns null and the body goes on; the archive call runs with null

origin.section: A do-while Fits a Loop Whose First Pass Produces What the Condition Tests

questions.stem: A test helper fills a bucket with `short tokens = 0; while (tokens < 40_000) tokens++;`. The largest short is 32,767. What does the loop do?

options.text: It never ends, since tokens++ takes 32,767 to -32,768 and the condition holds again
options.says: the counter wraps at the top of its type, and no short is 40,000 or more, so the exit doesn't exist

options.text: It never reaches 40,000 and throws, since tokens++ refuses to take 32,767 to 32,768
options.says: an increment past the top wraps without an error; nothing throws

options.text: It ends after 40,000 passes, since tokens++ takes 32,767 to 32,768 once the short is full
options.says: the variable keeps its type, and the value wraps to the bottom of its range

options.text: It ends after 32,767 passes, since tokens++ leaves 32,767 at 32,767 once the short is full
options.says: the value doesn't stick at the top: it wraps, and even a value stuck at 32,767 would keep the condition true

origin.section: A Loop Ends Only If Its Condition Can Become False for Every Input

questions.stem: Readings `{3, 8, 12, 15, 21}` are sorted, and we look for the first index with a reading above 10: `int lo = 0, hi = 4; while (lo <= hi) { int mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2; if (r[mid] > 10) hi = mid; else lo = mid + 1; } return lo;`. What does it return?

options.text: It never returns, since at lo = hi = 2 each pass probes index 2 and sets hi to 2
options.says: the condition comes from the convention whose updates move past mid, but hi = mid keeps it; at lo == hi nothing changes and the loop spins

options.text: It throws, since lo + (hi - lo) / 2 overflows and the probe at mid falls outside the array
options.says: low + (high - low) / 2 stays in range; it is (low + high) / 2 that can overflow

options.text: It returns 2, since <= instead of < only adds one more probe of index 2 at lo = hi = 2
options.says: with hi = mid the extra pass changes nothing, so it is not one more probe but the same probe forever

options.text: It returns 3, since <= lets lo move one index past the answer at lo = hi = 2
options.says: lo moves only past an index whose reading is not above 10; at lo == hi == 2 the reading is 12, so hi = mid and lo never moves

origin.section: The Invariant Decides the Condition, the Updates and the Midpoint

concepts: A do-while over input that may be empty runs its body once on nothing.
Taking <= from the closed-interval convention and high = mid from the other makes the search probe the last candidate forever.
